regions.Champaign-Urbana and East Central Illino: Start at home: two free university museums, Allerton's gardens on the Sangamon and Kickapoo's river valley make easy half days. Bloomington and the Amish towns of Arthur and Arcola round out a Saturday.
regions.Great River Road: The Mississippi bluffs between Nauvoo, Hannibal and Alton. Pair Elsah's stone village and Pere Marquette's lodge with Mark Twain's Hannibal across the river.
regions.Northern Illinois and Galena: A loop of modern architecture and river towns: Farnsworth House, Wright's Laurent House in Rockford, the John Deere and Reagan sites, then two nights in Galena for the bluffs and the Grant Home.
regions.Route 66 and the Illinois River: Follow old Route 66 north through Funks Grove and Pontiac to the Gemini Giant, then cut west to Starved Rock and Matthiessen for canyon hiking. Spring brings waterfalls, January brings eagles.
regions.Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio: Sandstone country in the Shawnee National Forest, cypress swamps on the Cache River, then across the Ohio to Paducah's quilt museum and Land Between the Lakes. Best in October.
regions.Springfield and Lincoln Country: A classic weekend. Spend one day on Lincoln (the Home, the Presidential Museum, the Old State Capitol and the Tomb) and the next on the Dana-Thomas House and New Salem, with a Route 66 lunch at the Cozy Dog.
regions.St. Louis Metro: Plan at least two days. Forest Park alone holds the free art and history museums; add the Gateway Arch, the Wainwright Building, the Pulitzer and the City Museum, and drive to Cahokia Mounds on the Illinois side.

sites.name: Krannert Art Museum
sites.desc: The University of Illinois art museum, free to all, with ancient Andean ceramics, African art, European paintings and contemporary work.

sites.name: Spurlock Museum of World Cultures
sites.desc: University museum of world cultures with galleries on Mesopotamia, Egypt, Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia.

sites.name: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts
sites.desc: Max Abramovitz's 1969 complex of four theaters around a grand brick lobby, one of the major performing arts centers of the Midwest.
sites.wiki: Krannert Center for the Performing Arts

sites.name: Museum of the Grand Prairie
sites.desc: Champaign County Forest Preserve museum in Mahomet on prairie life, Lincoln's circuit-riding years and local history.

sites.name: Robert Allerton Park
sites.desc: Robert Allerton's estate on the Sangamon River, given to the University of Illinois in 1946: formal gardens, the Fu Dog Garden and the Sun Singer within woods and prairie.

sites.name: Kickapoo State Recreation Area
sites.desc: Former strip-mine land regrown into forest and ponds on the Middle Fork of the Vermilion, Illinois's only National Wild and Scenic River.

sites.name: Lincoln Log Cabin State Historic Site
sites.desc: The farm of Thomas and Sarah Bush Lincoln, run as a living history farm of the 1840s near Charleston.
sites.wiki: Lincoln Log Cabin State Historic Site

sites.name: Big Things Small Town, Casey
sites.desc: A small town that turned itself into a roadside attraction with a dozen record-setting giant objects, from a wind chime to a mailbox.

sites.name: Arthur and Illinois Amish Country
sites.desc: The center of the largest Amish settlement in Illinois, with farm shops, bakeries and buggies on the county roads.

sites.name: David Davis Mansion
sites.desc: The 1872 Italianate villa of Lincoln's friend and Supreme Court justice David Davis in Bloomington, a state historic site.

sites.name: McLean County Museum of History
sites.desc: A regional history museum in the domed 1903 courthouse on Bloomington's square.

sites.name: Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum
sites.desc: Immersive galleries on Lincoln's life and a major research library of Lincoln and Illinois history, opened in 2005.
sites.wiki: Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum

sites.name: Lincoln Home National Historic Site
sites.desc: The only home Lincoln owned, where he lived from 1844 to 1861, in a restored four-block neighborhood.

sites.name: Dana-Thomas House
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie house for Susan Lawrence Dana (1902 to 1904), with its original art glass and furniture.

sites.name: Lincoln Tomb
sites.desc: Burial place of Abraham Lincoln, Mary Lincoln and three of their sons in Oak Ridge Cemetery.

sites.name: Old State Capitol
sites.desc: The Greek Revival capitol where Lincoln gave the House Divided speech in 1858.
sites.wiki: Old State Capitol State Historic Site

sites.name: Illinois State Capitol
sites.desc: The domed capitol completed in 1888, with free tours of its decorated chambers.

sites.name: Illinois State Museum
sites.desc: Natural history, archaeology and art of Illinois, from mastodons to Native American life and Illinois artists.

sites.name: Lincoln's New Salem
sites.desc: Reconstruction of the village where young Lincoln lived from 1831 to 1837.

sites.name: Cozy Dog Drive In
sites.desc: Route 66 diner in Springfield that claims the invention of the corn dog on a stick.

sites.name: Illinois Route 66 Hall of Fame and Museum
sites.desc: A Route 66 museum in Pontiac, surrounded by murals and memorabilia of the old highway.

sites.name: Funks Grove Pure Maple Sirup
sites.desc: Family maple syrup farm on old Route 66 near Shirley, still spelling sirup the old way.
sites.wiki: Funk's Grove Township, McLean County, Illinois

sites.name: Gemini Giant
sites.desc: A 1960s fiberglass Muffler Man astronaut standing on Route 66 in Wilmington.

sites.name: Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie
sites.desc: Restored tallgrass prairie on a former army arsenal near Wilmington, grazed by a bison herd.

sites.name: Starved Rock State Park
sites.desc: Sandstone canyons on the Illinois River with spring waterfalls, winter bald eagles and a 1930s CCC lodge.

sites.name: Matthiessen State Park
sites.desc: A quieter neighbor of Starved Rock with a deep dells canyon, stone bridges and falls.

sites.name: Peoria Riverfront Museum
sites.desc: Art, history and science museum with a planetarium on the Peoria riverfront.

sites.name: Wildlife Prairie Park
sites.desc: Park near Peoria with bison, elk, wolves and other native animals of Illinois in large habitats.

sites.name: Farnsworth House
sites.desc: Mies van der Rohe's glass house on the Fox River at Plano (1951), a defining work of modern domestic architecture.

sites.name: Illinois Railway Museum
sites.desc: One of the largest railway museums in the country, at Union, with operating trains on summer weekends.

sites.name: Laurent House
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's Usonian house in Rockford for Kenneth Laurent, a wheelchair user, and an early example of accessible design.

sites.name: Anderson Japanese Gardens
sites.desc: A celebrated Japanese garden in Rockford with ponds, waterfalls and a tea house.

sites.name: Burpee Museum of Natural History
sites.desc: Rockford museum best known for Jane, a juvenile Tyrannosaurus skeleton.

sites.name: Ronald Reagan Boyhood Home
sites.desc: The Dixon house where Reagan lived as a boy in the 1920s.

sites.name: John Deere Historic Site
sites.desc: Grand Detour, where John Deere built his self-scouring steel plow in 1837, with a working blacksmith shop.

sites.name: Galena Historic District
sites.desc: A 19th-century lead-mining boomtown of brick commercial streets in the hills above the Galena River.

sites.name: Ulysses S. Grant Home
sites.desc: The house Galena's citizens gave Grant on his return from the Civil War in 1865.

sites.name: Mississippi Palisades State Park
sites.desc: Limestone bluffs and overlooks above the Mississippi near Savanna.

sites.name: Bishop Hill
sites.desc: A Swedish Pietist colony founded in 1846, preserved as a village of colony buildings and museums.

sites.name: Black Hawk State Historic Site
sites.desc: Wooded bluffs in Rock Island with a museum of the Sauk and Meskwaki nations.

sites.name: Nauvoo Historic District
sites.desc: Mississippi River town built by Latter-day Saints from 1839 to 1846, with many restored houses and shops.

sites.name: Pere Marquette State Park
sites.desc: Bluffs at the meeting of the Illinois and Mississippi rivers, a CCC stone lodge and winter eagle watching.

sites.name: Elsah
sites.desc: A tiny 19th-century stone village tucked into a hollow of the Great River Road, entirely on the National Register.

sites.name: National Great Rivers Museum
sites.desc: Corps of Engineers museum at the Mel Price Locks and Dam, with lock tours.

sites.name: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site
sites.desc: Camp River Dubois, where the Corps of Discovery wintered in 1803 to 1804 before heading west.
sites.wiki: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site

sites.name: Cahokia Mounds
sites.desc: The largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, centered on Monks Mound. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sites.name: Chain of Rocks Bridge
sites.desc: The old Route 66 bridge over the Mississippi with its famous 22 degree bend, now open to walkers and cyclists.

sites.name: World's Largest Catsup Bottle
sites.desc: A 1949 water tower in Collinsville shaped like a giant catsup bottle.

sites.name: Garden of the Gods
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Wind-carved sandstone formations in the Shawnee National Forest with wide views over the hills.

sites.name: Giant City State Park
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Sandstone streets of giant bluffs and a CCC lodge near Carbondale.

sites.name: Cache River State Natural Area
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Cypress and tupelo swamps, with some of the oldest trees east of the Mississippi.

sites.name: Cave-In-Rock State Park
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A river cave on the Ohio once used by outlaws and river pirates.

sites.name: Superman statue, Metropolis
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: Metropolis embraces its name with a 15 foot Superman statue on the courthouse square.

sites.name: Fort de Chartres
sites.region: Southern Illinois and the Lower Ohio
sites.desc: A reconstructed 18th-century French stone fort in the American Bottom.
